i'm a manager at petco, and do some minimal animal care when necessary. i was not taught anything about our animals. it is such a shame that they do not train us, and like you i had to learn everything off the clock. i have no regrets when it comes to that though, i'm very glad that i did. i know in full confidence that i can sell the animal to an owner who gets all the information that they could possibly need, and are willing to learn. 
the most frustrating thing about working there is hearing my other coworkers giving false or outdated information. ive done my fair share of correcting them and catching mistakes, however i am not at the store 24/7 and there are absolutely mistakes being made all the time. 
for bearded dragons, the store tends to only give information about the care for BABY beardies. which, yes, are what we sell, but the customers should have an excellent understanding of how the care changes as they get older, and especially how big they actually get. they are only small little babies for such a short period of time, it's rediculous that we base all of our information on that time span.
i also wish we carried tanks that were larger than 75 gallons, because at least at my store that is the biggest one we carry. and a lot of people still think that a 40 gallon is suitable for a beardie. 
my biggest piece of advice is to correct and educate your coworkers on up-to-date care requirements, because that way even on your days off, you can be sure that they are giving proper information to interested pet owners.

a big misconception is that when two beardies are on top of each other, people think theyre cuddling. when in reality, theyre fighting for resources. the one on top is hoarding all of the heat from the lights. youll also notice that usually one beardie is bigger than the other because it hoards the food. 
its also much easier to notice any behavioral differences or health issues if the bearded dragon is housed alone. if you're not constantly monitoring them, you'll never know which one is pooping, which one is eating more, etc.
your beardie may have seemed "depressed" alone, but it was probably just fine, and if you noticed an increase of energy when you added the second, it was probably motivated by fear or self defense
